analysis.title: Datadog Inc. (DDOG) 3Q26: Puts and takes to AI scaling creates some sequential noise
key_insights: DDOG fell 14% on 11/4 after 3Q26 results. Revenue was 4% above the Street, EBIT margin was about 450bps above, and EPS was 26% above (FactSet).
4Q revenue was guided 0.6% below the Street, implying a revenue decline of about $2mn at the midpoint.

The guide reflects three items: Datadog is derisking its largest customer to minimum commitment after that customer was above minimum in 3Q, several large AI native and enterprise customers renewed early into higher volume discount tiers, and seasonality.

The new information is the early renewal pricing dynamic. Datadog has always offered volume discounts for higher minimum commitments, and customers have historically grown back into the revenue impact of a higher tier within one quarter.

AI native customers are scaling faster than customers did in the cloud cycle, which makes quarter-to-quarter revenue less predictable. GS reads the early renewals as coming from a position of strength in the customer base.
GS's key question at current stock levels is whether AI and new observability tools give customers more optionality for cost optimization and/or create incremental competitive pressure.
Datadog sees AI training as an emerging opportunity as model development expands beyond frontier labs. Internally it uses a mix of frontier, open weight and proprietary models.

Scout, Datadog's SRE-focused reasoning model, performs at or above frontier models for alert investigation at a fraction of the inference cost. GS thinks proprietary models may drive the next big product cycle with AI SRE.
GS maintains its Sell rating and raises the 12-month price target to $171 from $158, against a $188.72 price (9.4% downside).

market_movers.rationale: Sell maintained, target raised to $171 from $158 on 34x rolled-forward SNTM uFCF. The stock trades above the target, implying 9.4% downside.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported revenue $1,197mn vs GSe $1,141mn and Street $1,146mn (+4.9% vs GSe, +4.4% vs Street), up 35% y/y.
3Q26 reported non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.81 vs GSe $0.63 and Street $0.64 (+29.4% vs GSe, +26.2% vs Street), up 49% y/y.
3Q26 reported adjusted operating income $334mn vs GSe $265mn and Street $269mn, a 28% margin, about 447bps above Street.
3Q26 reported free cash flow $251mn vs GSe $232mn and Street $260mn (-3.7% vs Street), a 21% margin.
3Q26 reported gross profit $972mn, an 81% margin, vs Street $917mn (80% margin).
4Q26 revenue guidance is 0.6% below the Street (guidance, not a print), implying a roughly $2mn sequential decline at the midpoint.
GS quarterly EPS estimates: $0.69 for 12/26E, $0.72 for 3/27E, $0.77 for 6/27E (estimates).
risk_factors: Datadog spend at customers may go up before it goes down.
Datadog's product lead may be large enough to still win against cheaper competitors.
Datadog may pick up its pace of S&M investment to increase the quantum of NNARR in the model over the next 12-24 months.
AI and new observability tools could give customers more optionality for cost optimization or create incremental competitive pressure.
AI native customers scaling faster than cloud-cycle customers adds quarter-to-quarter unpredictability.

tension_points.bull_case: Early renewals come from a position of strength in the customer base, customers have historically grown back into a higher discount tier within one quarter, and Datadog's product lead may be large enough to win against cheaper competitors.
tension_points.bear_case: AI native customers scale faster and less predictably than cloud-cycle customers, early renewals move customers into higher discount tiers, and AI and new observability tools may give customers cost optimization optionality or add competitive pressure. GS rates the stock Sell with a $171 target below the $188.72 price.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Customer spend rising before it falls, or Datadog stepping up S&M investment to lift NNARR over the next 12-24 months (GS's stated risks to the Sell view).

theme_stances.key_argument: Early renewals into higher discount tiers and AI native scaling create sequential noise, and AI tools may give customers cost optimization optionality or add competition.
